nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: Why is it important to understand political institutions and actions in a cultural context?
nodes.answer: It is important because political activities are directed by interpretations and preferences rather than just bare facts and interests.
nodes.paragraph: Conflicts arise not only from clashing values and power imbalances (GI ck, 1994) but also from divergent perceptions (Hoogstra-Klein et al., 2012; Pokorny & Schanz, 2003). What is perceived as a problem, which solution becomes preferred by whom, and who bears the responsibility for both problems and solutions are central. Analyzing dis- agreements by investigating underlying conflicting worldviews is instrumental (Pokorny & Schanz, 2003). Several theoretical approaches or frameworks have been employed to study EU forest policy and its actors, such as discourse analysis/discursive agency (e.g., Leipold et al., 2016), Advocacy Coalition Framework (ACF), Shifting Coalitions Theory (SCT) (e.g. Sotirov et al., 2021), policy integration theories (e.g., P lzl et al., 2018), Multi-Level Governance (MLG) (e.g., P Izl et al., 2014), and Institutional Anal- ysis and Development (IAD) Framework (e.g., de Koning & Cleaver, 2012). According to Mamadouh (1999b), it is important to understand political institutions and actions in a cultural context, as political activities are directed by interpretations and prefer - ences, not by bare facts and interests.
